# STAT 4C03
```{r}
data = read.csv("Fastener.csv")
head(data)
```

# a)
```{r}
model.a = glm(
  cbind(Failed, Num.Fasteners - Failed) ~ Pressure,
  data = data,
  family = binomial
)
summ.a = summary(model.a)
summ.a
```
## Analysis result:
The results indicate that pressure has a significant positive effect on the probability of fastener failure. As pressure increases, the odds of failure increase, suggesting that higher pressure loads are associated with a greater risk of fastener failure.

# b)
```{r}
# Satured model
model.b = glm(
  cbind(Failed, Num.Fasteners - Failed) ~ factor(Pressure),
  data = data,
  family = binomial
)
summ.b = summary(model.b)
summ.b
```

```{r}
# fitted failure probabilities from both models
fitted.table <- data.frame(
  Pressure = data$Pressure,
  Saturated = predict(model.b, type = "response"),
  Logistic  = predict(model.a, type = "response")
)

fitted.table
```
# c)
```{r}
# Extract variables
x  <- fitted.table$Pressure
pS <- fitted.table$Saturated
pL <- fitted.table$Logistic

# Plot the saturated model curve
plot(x, pS,
     type = "b",      # both points and lines
     lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Pressure",
     ylab = "Failure probability",
     main = "Failure Probability Curves")

# Add the logistic model curve
lines(x, pL,
      type = "b",
      col="red",
      pch = 17,
      lwd = 2)

# Add legend
legend("bottomright",
       legend = c("Saturated model", "Logistic model"),
       lwd = 2)
```
The two curves are almost exactly the same with slight differences.

# d)
```{r}
# Computing the deviance 
ni = data$Num.Fasteners
pi.hat.i = model.a$fitted.values
yi = data$Failed

D = 2 * sum( yi * log( yi / (ni * pi.hat.i) ) + (ni - yi) * log( (ni - yi) / (ni * (1 - pi.hat.i)) ) )
cat("Computed deviance =", D, "model.a's deviance =", model.a$deviance)
```
We have exactly the same value of the deviance, the results agree.

# e)
```{r}
# Pearson GOF statistic

X2 <- sum((yi - ni*pi.hat.i)^2 / (ni*pi.hat.i*(1 - pi.hat.i)))

n  <- length(yi) # number of observations
p  <- 1 # estimated parameters
df <- n - p - 1 # degree of freedom

p_value <- 1 - pchisq(X2, df)

cat("Pearson X2 =", X2, "\n")
cat("p-value =", p_value, "\n")
```

```{r}
# The deviance GOF p-value
p_value = 1 - pchisq(D, df)
cat("p-value =", p_value, "\n")
```
The Pearson and deviance goodness-of-fit tests both yield large p-values around 0.99. There is no evidence against the fitted binomial regression model. The model appears to provide an adequate fit to the data.

# f)
```{r}
# The model with no covariate
model.f = glm(
  cbind(Failed, Num.Fasteners - Failed) ~ 1,
  data = data,
  family = binomial
)

# LRT 
anova(model.a, model.f)
```
The value of the test sttatistic is
G2 =112.83207 − 0.37192= 112.46015
Under H0 (Pressure has no effect of the the probability of failure), G2 follows chi2(1)
The corresponding p-value is p-value = 2.2e-16
## Conclusion
Since the p-value is extremely small, we reject the null hypothesis. There is an overwhelming evidence that pressure significantly affects the probability of failure.
